title: CharForge: rigged, animated game characters from a few words or one image, on a laptop
subtitle: A living research paper - method, measurements and open problems, revised as the experiments run
acknowledgement: Experiments and this living paper were developed with Claude (Anthropic) working in the repository. Script-backed values are included where artifacts exist; some historical and prose claims remain manually maintained and are being audited.

changes: Faces in parts (E140), on a benchmark set of two characters per style per gender instead of the whole roster (Mara, Juno, Rowan, Knight; Vex, Rivet, Pip, Cadet; Aoi, Hana, Kaito, Ren), scored by a new face measure: landmark error against the picture after one similarity and per-part DINOv3 likeness of face, eyes, nose and mouth (section 5.8, Table: faces).

Eyes rebuilt as lids over an eyeball: TRELLIS.2 models every eye as an opening full of shards; each opening is found by DWPose on the generator's own paint and rebuilt in the solid, and the head keeps 28% of the triangle budget (Figure: eyes).

The face laid on in parts - each brow, eye, the nose, mouth and jaw moved by its own similarity onto the model's own points, spread by a thin-plate spline - replacing the face flow; the face's ellipse painted by the front view alone and left out of the skin tone (Figure: face in parts). The face flow, keeping the generator's face, and the skin tone over the face moved to the archive.
The generator's black chart-edge specks taken out before the bake; new characters generated with a 2048 px texture; the jaw's cut held to 0.8 of the eye spacing.
New negative results: more head texels, landmarks on grey renders, an eyeball in the mesh, eyes found from the picture or as depth pits, a vertex group at weight 0.
References: Umeyama 1991, Bookstein 1989, Garland and Heckbert 1997.

Toward a professionally made model: a model-quality audit (E132) - surface noise and lumps, triangle tilt, asymmetry about the best mirror plane, open edges and loose pieces, lighting left in the albedo, front/back colour, seams, the PBR range - run on every character and on professionally made meshes (Blender Studio's Human Base Meshes and Ellie from Sprite Fright), and eight lit close-ups of every character (E138). New section 5.7 and Table 10; the roster was rebuilt on what they found.

A finer surface (E135): TRELLIS.2 keeps 1M faces instead of 200k, and the generated surface is filtered by bilateral normal filtering before anything is built on it - the triangle pattern the facets left in the normal map is gone (Figure: raking light, v0.11 against v0.12).

The pose it was modelled in, as the rest pose (E137): the T is recorded for the retargeting maths instead of being baked into the mesh by skinning; on Cadet crushed faces 3.44% -> 1.45%, self-intersecting face pairs 1,093 -> 502 a frame, frames with a limb 2 cm inside another 40% -> 28%, foot slip unchanged. --rest T keeps the old way; the manifest says which.

Close-up faults mended (E138): loose shards dropped from every low-poly (2-94 a character); modelled hands shaded from their own ambient occlusion instead of a colour bake of the generated mesh (two-tone patches gone); one skin tone at the 1-2 cm scale of shading (Mara's wrist ring dE 16.6 -> 1.5); non-metal colours kept in the PBR range (sRGB 30-240); the face flow on realistic faces only - on the finer mesh it dragged Pip's drawn eye into a second one.

Faces (E139): a head made again on its own from a crop of the picture by Hunyuan3D 2.1's shape model has the picture's shape where the whole-figure model's is a few facets; it is joined to the body above the neck and painted from the front - an option (--head hunyuan), not yet the default.

Measured and set aside: Hunyuan3D-Paint 2.1's own bake on Apple Silicon and its views as every character's sides and back (better on Pip, worse by eye on 6 of 8; an option, --texture-views hunyuan) (E134); delighting the reference on its own (E133); delighting the face close-up; quad remeshing (refused our meshes); the head generated alone by TRELLIS.2 (over 30 minutes) - in the negative results.

Archive: the 200k-face surface, the T baked into the rest pose and the hands shaded from the colour bake moved to Appendix D. The Studio gained Rest pose, Sides and back and Head options; the playground shows all fourteen characters.

Moves from words (E129): UniMate generates a move from a sentence on the character's own skeleton - flow matching conditioned on its topology and T-pose - in about 25 s on Apple's GPU with a fixed Euler grid; three samples, one chosen by eye, then retargeted, planted and held inside the joint limits like any clip. Cadet has five, and a bow made from the Studio's new Moves from words panel; on the surface they fall inside his captured clips' range. tools/setup_unimate.sh installs it.

The shoe the viewer sees is the one planted (E130): every vertex of the shoe below the ankle, posed by its own skin weights with dual quaternions, replaces a rigid copy of the sole on the ankle bone. Cadet's frames with a boot more than 1 cm under the floor 48.3% -> 1.28%; on 13 characters x 9 gaits the worse foot's median slip 4.01% -> 2.89%. Thinning the shoe to 400 points made 12 gaits worse by more than a point (the pivot jumped between samples) and is not used.

Foot slip is reported from the true-speed audit (metric v2) on all 14 characters: median 3.2%, worst 28.4% - Cadet's sprint, whose flared greaves are planted as if they were the sole (E131); 2.89% without him. The old table, which divided by at least 1 m/s, moved to a new Appendix D, Archive, with the rigid sole it measured.

A new character, Cadet (stylised, a young space marine without emblems), made with the pipeline as it stands; the prompt writer had read 'about 19 years old' as elderly - fixed. The system overview gains the words lane, the abstract the aberration audit, and armour's large joint-limit corrections are attributed to Cadet's knees.
The lab notebook leads with the aberration audit, the planted shoe, moves from words and Cadet, and archives the methods they replaced: the second 3D pass, the rigid sole and the old foot-slip table.

A programme for shape and texture as clean as a professional's, registered before it runs: a model-quality audit against professional baselines (Blender Studio's CC0 Human Base Meshes, Ellie from Sprite Fright) (E132), then the reference's lighting removed before projection (E133), sides and back painted by a multi-view PBR model (E134), quad remeshing with baked detail (E135) and detail from estimated normals (E136); E131 plants the shoe's contact patch.

The aberration audit runs and is validated (E102): 22 of 22 checks on a synthetic character with known-size aberrations pass under both skinnings, penetration to the millimetre; the checks exposed three measuring errors (quads re-split by pose, depth capped at 3 cm, false inside readings at open rims and between layers), now fixed. Blender's BVH overlap is a triangle-triangle test, so intersections are real; depth tells contact from penetration.

The roster measured on every frame of every clip: crushed 2.72%, stretched 1.52%, sheared 2.71% of faces; dual quaternion against linear skinning; frames with a body region more than 2 cm inside another 48.44%.

Joint limits measured on each character's own mesh, and every clip held inside them (E128): frames with deep penetration 48.44% -> 34.28%, surface measures and foot slip unchanged. New related work: contact-aware retargeting.

Time (E106 pilot): the multi-view second 3D pass fitted the reference's front worse on 12 of 12 characters and drifted from the picture where its repainted views invented detail; it is now off by default, saving a median 16 of 41 minutes. The end-to-end comparison is still to run.

Audited legacy citations against primary sources: separated the pinned Mixamo mirror count from Adobe's product page, corrected hand-deformation and skinning citations, distinguished Qwen-Image 2.1's checkpoint/license from earlier papers, and narrowed vendor claims.

Recorded TRELLIS.2 research-only materials, the unresolved H3 fine-tune/base-license conflict, and Mixamo mirror access/redistribution uncertainty; added primary license sources and corrected method, limitations, README, and E115 provenance language.
Reconciled E102 prose with current code safeguards (topology/order assertion, centered pop metric, default no-clobber); no Blender runtime validation or new experiment result was performed.
Added primary-source references for stylized AU controls, segmentation reliability, and footskate perception; explicitly limit transfer claims and thresholds.

Tightened planned metric definitions and acceptance protocols for motion truth, dense aberration sampling, scan/retopo distance, part-label calibration, hand pose, runtime delivery, foot-contact parity, provenance/cache validity, and Studio workflows.

Recorded that the browser footAudit still uses a 1 m/s denominator floor and differs in contact sampling from the corrected Blender v2 path; historical results remain unchanged and E122 remains required.

Added the user-requested fast-classifier investigation as E127 at the end of the queue. Model identity, architecture and license remain unverified; discovery and benchmarking are explicitly gated behind earlier queued work.

Research-gap audit across prompt fidelity, geometry repair, part labels, retopology, UVs, runtime texture sampling, deformation, motion truth, engine delivery, provenance and evaluation; added primary-source references and planned experiments E116-E126.

Reopened E029 after finding its legacy max(speed, 1 m/s) denominator understated sub-1 m/s ratios; preserved historical measurements and specified a corrected rerun. E102's candidate-only BVH and cadence-specific pop measures are documented; code changes remain pending Blender runtime validation.
Clarified that the paper build validates references and structure but does not yet link every manually maintained empirical claim to an artifact; E121 tracks that work.

The lab book became this paper: method, evaluation with every number collected from the measurement files (paper/collect.py), related work with verified references, limitations and a roadmap; the chronological lab notebook kept beside it.
Experiment tracker (research/experiments.json, rendered as research/TRACKER.md and Appendix A).

Multi-angle verification (E009) found an elbow folded through the arm (E007), feet off the floor (E008), a comparison video running 25% fast (E010), and showed the kick's score dip was the scorer (E011).

Characters from a few words (E014-E016); hands that meet a bare forearm (E021) and take the face's colour (E020); a realistic face kept from the generator when the reference cannot be laid on it (E022); face positions read at 0.5 mm (E019).
The polish pass: garments fused to the body (E025), folded UV islands (E027), references in the wrong pose (E028), joins left by the arm cut (E026, open).
Hands follow DWPose (E006); the Studio, a local interface to make characters without the command line.
Moves from generated video: retrieval (E001), the fit (E002, E003), aimed limbs (E004), the refine stage (E005); H3 on 24 GB (E030).
Qwen-Image 2.1 as the reference model (E013); three styles, seven characters, the v3.0.0 site.
One entry point, engine conventions (origin, capsule, LODs), real PBR; locomotion that plants its feet (E029).
A local text-to-rigged-character pipeline with its first measurements; dual quaternion skinning in the viewer (E024).
